newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - March 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - March 26.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- Chinese Premier Li Peng and U.S. Vice-President Al Gore meet in Beijing, preside over Sino-U.S. forum on environment
- Li says he hopes Gore's visit will further boost Sino-U.S. ties
- China has issued 31.148 billion yuan of certified state bonds from March 1 to March 20
- In 1995, China had 520,000 registered drug addicts
- Supreme People's Court announces death sentences on three bank robbers
FINANCIAL NEWS
- Chen Yuan, deputy governor of central bank, says bank faces arduous task in supervision in 1997, financial risk will have impact on economy if unresolved
- Bank of Montreal to open Beijing branch on April 3
- China's to 10 industrial firms make profits that account for 52.4 percent of total profits of 15,000 firms
- China Huayang United Leasing Co Ltd, renamed as Huayang Financial Leasing Co Ltd
CHINA SECURITIES
- Central bank governor Dai Xianglong says inflation to be under 6.0 percent in 1997
- Official of State Commission for Economic Restructuring says more state firms should adopt share-holding system
- Editorial says conditions for over-the-counter trading not ripe
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH
- President Jiang Zemin says confident in future of Macau
- China punishes officials for selling government posts
CHINA DAILY

- Foreign Ministry spokesman stresses China will never tolerate any attempts to split the nation, criticises recent separatist activities of Dalai lama, Taiwan authorities and overseas Uighur separatists
